title: Many Americans Won't Travel Without Their Pets
paragraphs: Choosing where to go, how to get there and how long to stay are all normal parts of planning a trip. But for many pet owners, there's another important question: Can my pet come, too?
A new survey of 2,000 US dog and cat owners shows that pets are having a big influence on the way their owners travel — and, for some, whether they travel at all!
The survey, done by Talker Research in July 2026, found that 45% of pet owners had said no to a trip because they couldn't bring their pet with them.

And when they do leave their animals at home, they usually don't want to stay away too long. Thirty-one percent said they limit trips without their pets to just a day or two. Another 37% said they can manage a few days, but start to feel uneasy after that.
Nearly half said they feel bad when they travel without their pet, and the same percentage said they worry about their furry friends while they're away.

That's probably why many are willing to change how they travel so their pets can come along. Seven in ten said they were more likely to take a road trip instead of flying if it meant they could bring their pet. And almost half said they wouldn't mind driving more than four hours for the same reason.
And for many, all that extra effort may just be worth it, with around half saying that traveling with a pet is better than traveling with another person!
